item.title: How Iran Adapted Its Attacks as U.S. War Munitions Dwindled
item.description: The Iranian strikes that killed three U.S. soldiers in Jordan show how quickly Iran’s war-fighting skills have evolved, as the Pentagon runs low on interceptors.
item.dc:creator: Eric Schmitt and Helene Cooper
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:credit: -/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
item.media:description: Iran has become a more skilled adversary as its war against the United States has progressed, learning how to evade U.S. air defenses as it widened the battlefield to include most of the Middle East.

item.title: University of Michigan Will Ease Up on Grades for Student Mental Health
item.description: The University of Michigan will make first-semester grades pass or fail, to encourage students to try different classes and lessen fears of what a low grade could mean.
item.dc:creator: Mark Arsenault
item.media:credit: Sylvia Jarrus for The New York Times
item.media:description: The grade changes at the University of Michigan will go into effect in fall of 2027.

item.title: With El-Sayed’s Victory Comes a Wave of Islamophobia
item.description: As Muslim politicians like Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan have become more prominent, they have experienced considerable bigotry. President Trump said Democrats were electing “jihadists.”
item.dc:creator: Jennifer Medina
item.media:credit: Nick Hagen for The New York Times
item.media:description: Since Dr. Abdul El-Sayed’s victory in the Democratic Senate primary in Michigan last week, Republicans have embraced Islamophobic attacks and falsehoods.

item.title: Trump Picks Project 2025 Co-Author for Role That Would Oversee Any Reflecting Pool Review
item.description: Dennis Kirk, a former adviser to Tulsi Gabbard, is President Trump’s nominee for inspector general for the Interior Department.

item.media:description: The Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool.

item.title: U.S. Says It Revoked More Than 175,000 Visas Under Trump
item.description: Most visas were rescinded over criminal accusations, the State Department said, while some were revoked from people who had celebrated the assassination of Charlie Kirk.
item.dc:creator: Isabella Kwai
item.media:credit: Nathan Howard for The New York Times
item.media:description: The State Department’s release did not include names or details of where people were when their visas were revoked.

item.title: Wildfire Forces Evacuations in Big Sur, Along California’s Famed Coast
item.description: A fire broke out near Highway 1 on Sunday and spread rapidly overnight, prompting evacuation orders across Monterey County.
item.dc:creator: Jin Yu Young and Maia Spoto
item.media:credit: Tayfun Coskun/Anadolu, via Getty Images
item.media:description: A firefighter battled flames from a wildfire near Big Sur, Calif., on Monday.

item.title: Democrats Plan New Push to Defeat Max Miller in Ohio After Abuse Accusations
item.description: The party’s congressional campaign arm added Mr. Miller’s opponent, Brian Poindexter, to its highly competitive “Red to Blue” list.
item.dc:creator: Emily Davies
item.media:credit: Daniel Lozada for The New York Times
item.media:description: Brian Poindexter is the type of candidate Democrats believe can win over working-class voters who have flocked to President Trump in recent years.

item.title: Can Immigration Agents Stop People Based on Appearance?
item.description: Jazmine Ulloa, our national reporter covering immigration, describes body-camera footage and other court evidence that federal agents used slurs and racially profiled people during immigration sweeps.
item.dc:creator: Jazmine Ulloa, Nour Idriss, Gilad Thaler, Stephanie Swart, June Kim and Bernardo Garcia Elguezabal

item.title: What to Watch in Tuesday’s Primary Elections in Wisconsin, Minnesota and South Carolina
item.description: The left and the middle continue to battle in Democratic primaries for governor in Wisconsin and Senate in Minnesota. In South Carolina, all eyes are on Darline Graham.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Mazzei
item.media:credit: Alex Kent/The New York Times
item.media:description: Senator Darline Graham, who was appointed to complete the remainder of the late Senator Lindsey Graham’s term, is also running to succeed her brother for a full term. She faces four others in the special Republican primary.

item.title: New Evidence Shows Federal Agents Using Racial Slurs During Immigration Sweeps
item.description: Body-camera video and other court evidence capture federal agents using slurs and targeting Latinos while bypassing white bystanders during immigration sweeps in Chicago and Los Angeles
item.dc:creator: Jazmine Ulloa, Maia Spoto and Jill Cowan
item.media:credit: David Guttenfelder/The New York Times
item.media:description: Federal agents making an arrest in Minneapolis in January.

item.title: Jake Whisenant, Who Raced Up Yosemite’s El Capitan at Record Speed, Dies in a Fall
item.description: Authorities in California said he died in a climbing accident. He set a record in 2024 for climbing El Capitan’s Lurking Fear route in under three hours.
item.dc:creator: Francesca Regalado
item.media:credit: Loren Elliott for The New York Times
item.media:description: El Capitan in Yosemite National Park last year. Jake Whisenant set a speed record on its Lurking Fear route in 2024.

item.title: Californians Criticize Federal Efforts to Control the State’s Coast
item.description: Environmentalists and others warned at a hearing on Monday that the Trump administration’s attempt to strip power from California’s coastal protection agency would endanger the shoreline.
item.dc:creator: Livia Albeck-Ripka
item.media:credit: Loren Elliott for The New York Times
item.media:description: The coastline in Pacifica, Calif.

item.title: Homeland Security Intensifies Pursuit of Noncitizens on Voter Rolls
item.description: Immigrants who said they inadvertently registered to vote while obtaining or renewing driver’s licenses are increasingly facing deportation under the Trump administration.
item.dc:creator: Madeleine Ngo, Nick Corasaniti and Hamed Aleaziz
item.media:credit: Nick Hagen for The New York Times
item.media:description: In the past, the Homeland Security Department has not aggressively tried to deport the relatively small number of noncitizens who unlawfully registered to vote.
